'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[Bombing of Odesa (2022–present)|Bombing of Odesa]]
***A nighttime Russian missile attack on [[Odesa]] kills at least one person, injures 22 others, and severely damages the [[Transfiguration Cathedral in Odesa|Transfiguration Cathedral]]. [https://apnews.com/article/odesa-missile-grain-deal-ukraine-russia-adc78b45e74e0236125b1ec706e5d7da (AP)]
**[[Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant crisis]]
***The [[International Atomic Energy Agency]] finds [[anti-personnel mine]]s at the Russian-occupied [[Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant]], but notes that any detonation "should not affect the site's nuclear safety and security systems". [https://www.barrons.com/news/mines-found-at-ukraine-s-zaporizhzhia-nuclear-plant-un-watchdog-9ad63a7d (AFP via ''Barron's'')] [https://www.iaea.org/newscenter/pressreleases/update-175-iaea-director-general-statement-on-situation-in-ukraine (IAEA)]
*[[Sistan and Baluchestan insurgency]]
**At least four road patrol policemen are killed in an [[ambush]] in [[Zahedan]], [[Sistan and Baluchestan province]], [[Iran]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/least-four-dead-attack-irans-zahedan-tasnim-2023-07-23/ (Reuters)]

'''Business and economy'''
*A deal to sell a controlling interest in the Israeli financial firm [[Phoenix Group]] to a consortium led by an [[Abu Dhabi]] state holding company is federally averted. [https://www.reuters.com/markets/deals/sale-control-israels-phoenix-adq-led-group-falls-through-2023-07-23/ (Reuters)]
 
'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2023 Raigad landslide]]
**The death toll from the [[landslide]] in [[Raigad district|Raigad]], [[Maharashtra]], [[India]], increases to 27, with at least 50 people still missing, as [[Monsoon of South Asia|monsoon]] rains complicate rescue efforts. [https://www.dawn.com/news/1766362/death-toll-of-landslide-in-indias-maharashtra-state-jumps-to-27-at-least-50-missing (AFP via ''Dawn'')]
*[[2023 Greece wildfires]]
**[[Emergency evacuation]]s by boat take place in [[Corfu]] as [[wildfire]]s rapidly spread in just a few hours, especially in the [[North Corfu|north of the island]]. [https://www.mirror.co.uk/news/world-news/breaking-corfu-evacuated-devastating-rhodes-30535719 (Mirror)]
**Thousands of tourists flee their hotels in [[Rhodes]], [[Greece]], in what officials say is the largest evacuation in the country's history. [https://edition.cnn.com/2023/07/22/europe/greece-record-breaking-heat-wave-climate-intl/index.html (CNN)]
*[[Flash flood]]s in [[Afghanistan]]'s [[Kabul Province| Kabul]], the [[Ghazni Province|Ghazni]] and [[Maidan Wardak Province|Maidan Wardak]] provinces, have killed at least 31 people, injured 74 others, and left 41 missing in the past three days. Around 250 [[livestock]] are also killed. In neighboring [[Pakistan]], thirteen people are also killed due to heavy rains and [[landslide]]s. [https://apnews.com/article/rain-floods-afghanistan-be47a5732198909836a9f855074289d1 (AP)]
*At least 33 people are killed and 21 others are injured when a [[Structural integrity and failure|building collapses]] in [[Douala]], [[Cameroon]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-66285325 (BBC News)]
*Eleven people are killed and three injured after a school's roof collapses in [[Qiqihar]], [[Heilongjiang]], [[China]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2023/7/24/girls-playing-netball-killed-as-school-gym-collapses-in-china (Al Jazeera)]
*Nine people, including four [[Sudanese Armed Forces|soldiers]], are killed when a civilian [[Antonov]] aircraft crashes due to technical issues in [[Port Sudan]], [[Sudan]]. A child is the [[List of sole survivors of aviation accidents and incidents|sole survivor]] of the crash. [https://www.thedailystar.net/news/world/news/nine-killed-civilian-plane-crash-sudan-war-hit-capital-left-hungry-3377161 (AFP via ''The Daily Star'')]
*Eight people are killed after people siphoning fuel from a tanker that was involved in an accident explodes in [[Ondo State]], [[Nigeria]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/fuel-truck-explosion-kills-8-southern-nigeria-2023-07-24/ (Reuters)]
*One person is killed and 12 others are injured after a bridge collapses in [[Patras]], [[Greece]]. [https://greekcitytimes.com/2023/07/24/safety-manager-and-three-employees-arrested-after-deadly-bridge-collapse-in-greece/ (Greek City Times)]

'''International relations'''
*[[2023 Quran desecration in Sweden]]
**The [[Organisation of Islamic Cooperation]] suspends [[Sweden]]'s [[special envoy]] in response to incidents of [[Quran desecration]] during public demonstrations permitted by the [[Government of Sweden|Swedish government]] in [[Stockholm]]. [https://apnews.com/article/sweden-quran-burning-organization-islamic-cooperation-96f79d096af6ed8e41930c34588ff0ba (AP)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[List of mass shootings in the United States in 2023]]
**A pregnant woman is killed and four others are injured in a mass shooting in a city park of [[Houston]], [[Texas]], United States. Two suspects are arrested. [https://people.com/21-year-old-pregnant-woman-killed-4-injured-in-texas-shooting-police-7564449 (''People'')]
*[[Gun violence in the United States]]
**Six people are killed and 20 others are injured in shootings across [[Chicago]], [[Illinois]], [[United States]]. [https://news.yahoo.com/weekend-shootings-leave-least-6-155502382.html (Yahoo! News)]
*A soldier kills 13 people, including ten children, during a [[mass shooting]] at his son's funeral in Nyamamba, [[Ituri Province]], [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2023/7/24/soldier-in-dr-congo-kills-wife-dozen-mourners-at-sons-funeral (Al Jazeera)]
*Two people are killed and four more injured during a mass shooting in [[Manta, Ecuador|Manta]], [[Ecuador]]. The city's mayor is among the killed. [https://apnews.com/article/ecuador-mayor-killed-gun-attack-1db25874b6882c6c9f54c96ce9e4e452 (AP)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2023 Spanish general election]]
**[[Spain|Spaniards]] head to the polls to elect the members of the [[Cortes Generales]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/spain-heads-close-run-polls-marked-by-spectre-far-right-2023-07-23/ (Reuters)]
**[[Alberto Núñez Feijóo]]'s [[People's Party (Spain)|People's Party]] wins the election, but falls short of a clear majority, while [[Prime Minister of Spain|Prime Minister]] [[Pedro Sánchez]]'s [[Spanish Socialist Workers' Party|Socialist Workers' Party]] holds slightly more seats with its allies despite finishing second, thus resulting in a [[hung parliament]]. [https://apnews.com/article/election-right-left-coalition-franco-spain-83cad969eac6cf25ced972357a248e99 (AP)]
*[[2023 Cambodian general election]]
**[[Cambodia]]ns head to the polls to elect the members of the [[Parliament of Cambodia|parliament]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/cambodia-holds-lopsided-election-ahead-historic-transfer-power-2023-07-22/ (Reuters)]
**The ruling [[Cambodian People's Party]], led by [[Prime Minister of Cambodia|Prime Minister]] [[Hun Sen]], claims a [[landslide victory]] in the election, winning 120 out of 125 seats according to unofficial results, despite criticism over alleged [[Political repression|suppression]] of the [[Opposition (politics)|opposition]]. [https://apnews.com/article/cambodia-elections-hun-sen-bc3b5f71d1f1fcaab3d246aed7ba5eeb (AP)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2022–23 PGA Tour]]
**[[2023 Open Championship]]
***[[Golf in the United States|American golfer]] [[Brian Harman]] wins his first [[The Open Championship|Open Championship]], his first career [[Men's major golf championships|major championship]], and his first [[PGA Tour]] win in six years, by six shots over [[Golf in Australia|Australia]]'s [[Jason Day]], [[Golf in South Korea|South Korea]]'s [[Tom Kim]], [[Sport in Spain|Spain]]'s [[Jon Rahm]], and [[Sport in Austria|Austria]]'s [[Sepp Straka]]. [https://apnews.com/article/harman-british-open-claret-jug-major-royal-liverpool-ef773f589855f285355c6634d502f422 (AP)]
*[[2023–24 SailGP championship]]
**In [[Sailing (sport)|sailing]], [[Royal Spanish Sailing Federation|Spain]] win their first [[SailGP]] championship in the [[Los Angeles]] Sail Grand Prix in [[California]], United States. [https://apnews.com/article/botin-spain-sailgp-ellison-foiling-catamarans-3cd8446628bf916aad962375c66152b8 (AP)]
*[[2023 World Aquatics Championships]]
**In the [[Swimming at the 2023 World Aquatics Championships – Men's 400 metre individual medley|men's 400 metre individual medley]], [[France at the 2023 World Aquatics Championships|French]] [[Swimming at the 2023 World Aquatics Championships|swimmer]] [[Léon Marchand]] breaks the longstanding [[World record progression 400 metres individual medley|world record]] previously set by American swimmer [[Michael Phelps]], finishing in 4 minutes, 2.5 seconds. [https://www.channelstv.com/2023/07/23/marchand-smashes-phelps-last-remaining-world-record/ (AFP via Channels TV)]
*[[2023 FIVB Volleyball Men's Nations League]]
**Hosts [[Poland men's national volleyball team|Poland]] win their first [[FIVB Volleyball Men's Nations League|VNL]] title after defeating the [[United States men's national volleyball team|United States]] 3–1 in the final at the [[Ergo Arena]] in [[Gdańsk]]. [https://en.volleyballworld.com/volleyball/competitions/vnl-2023/news/poland-claim-historic-vnl-gold-in-front-of-their-home-fans (Volleyball World)]
